slides.say: A train three hundred meters long travels at a constant speed. It passes a signal post in fifteen seconds. How many seconds does it take to cross a bridge five hundred meters long completely?
at: A train three hundred meters long

slides.say: So the train has a length, and they ask for the time on the bridge. The speed isn't given, so the post gives it to us.
We'll solve it in two different ways. Let's start with the math way, like in the lesson. Passing a post, the train moves its own length, three hundred meters, in fifteen seconds.
at: three hundred meters, in fifteen seconds

slides.say: The speed is three hundred divided by fifteen, twenty meters a second.

slides: Next, we use the speed of twenty meters a second on the bridge.

slides.say: Now the bridge. It starts when the front gets on the bridge, and ends when the back gets off.
So the front moves the bridge plus one train length. Five hundred plus three hundred is eight hundred meters.
Eight hundred divided by twenty is forty seconds.
Twenty-five, choice number one, divides only the bridge. It forgets the train's own length.
[pause] Now by understanding, with ratios. We start again from the givens. The speed is the same the whole time, so the time and the distance go the same way.
Three hundred meters take fifteen seconds. So a hundred meters take a third of that, five seconds.
at: So a hundred meters take a third

slides.say: Crossing the bridge completely, the front moves the bridge plus the train, eight hundred meters. That's eight hundreds, so eight times five, forty seconds.
Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
